1.1.text:
Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER XII
SANCTIONS
Article 41
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of providing protection, that does not carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 26
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c constitutes services provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who require continuous handling.
(3) Special social rehabilitation for female victims of domestic violence and human trafficking is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
(4) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus having principal tasks and functions in the fields of:
a. social affairs;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
(5) In addition to being implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation may also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Garut Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regent is the Regent of Garut.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in administering government affairs that are the authority of the Regency region.
6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom.
11. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household scope.
15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
16. Guardian is a person or entity that in fact exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations.
19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service.
20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Garut Regency area.
21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect.
22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect.
23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
27. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions properly.
28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
30. Integrated Service Center for Women Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated service center in efforts to empower women in various fields of development, as well as protection of women and children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, established by the Government or community-based, which includes: referral centers, business consultation centers, reproductive health consultation centers, legal consultation centers, Integrated Crisis Centers (PKT), Integrated Service Centers (PPT), trauma recovery centers (trauma centers), women's crisis handling centers (women crisis centers), training centers, Science and Technology Information Centers (PIPTEK), safe houses (shelters), transit houses, or other forms.
31. Women and Child Protection Task Force is a functional Work Unit that organizes integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women at the Sub-district level.
32. Women and Child Protection Task Unit is a functional Work Unit that organizes integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women at the Village/Sub-district level.

Article 27
Women's empowerment as referred to in Article 15 letter d, includes:
a. improving life resilience;
b. improving economic enterprises; and
c. increasing women's participation as builders, mediators and peace negotiators.

14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household scope.

16. Guardian is a person or entity that in fact exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child.

18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations.
19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service.
20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Garut Regency area.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

3. Regent is the Regent of Garut.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is a regional people's representative institution positioned as an element of regional government administration.
5. Regency Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and Regency DPRD in administering government affairs that are the authority of the Regency region.
6. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and children victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention efforts, services and social rehabilitation.
7. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child still in the womb.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality.
9. Protection of Children is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually, and/or neglect, including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom.
11. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household scope.
15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
16. Guardian is a person or entity that in fact exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
18. Community is individuals, families, groups, and/or community organizations.
19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service.
20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Garut Regency area.
21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect.
22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect.
23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
26. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions in order to carry out their role again properly both in the family and in society.
27. Social Rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions properly.
28. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
29. Legal Aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to conduct the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender sensitive.
30. 31. Women and Child Protection Task Force is a functional Work Unit that organizes integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women at the Sub-district level.
32. Women and Child Protection Task Unit is a functional Work Unit that organizes integrated protection services and handling of cases of violence against children and women at the Village/Sub-district level.

Article 3
The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in carrying out prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and children victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER XII
SANCTIONS
Article 41
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of providing protection, that does not carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 36
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are set forth in the form of agreements in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 13
(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.
(2) Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (1), include: a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.

Article 26
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c constitutes services provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who require continuous handling.
(3) Special social rehabilitation for female victims of domestic violence and human trafficking is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
(4) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus having principal tasks and functions in the fields of:
a. social affairs;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
(5) In addition to being implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation may also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

CHAPTER VII
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM VIOLENCE

Article 14
(1) Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 10 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims.
(2) In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may transfer to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 13
(1) The community as referred to in Article 10 letter c has the obligation and responsibility for the protection of women and children through community participation activities in the protection of women and children.

CHAPTER VII
IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM VIOLENCE

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 26
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c constitutes services provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.
(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who require continuous handling.
(3) Special social rehabilitation for female victims of domestic violence and human trafficking is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
(4) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus having principal tasks and functions in the fields of:
a. social affairs;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
(5) In addition to being implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation may also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

CHAPTER XII
SANCTIONS
Article 41
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of providing protection, that does not carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 39
(1) Reporting on the implementation of protection for women and children from violence shall be conducted by:
a. P2TP2A to the Regent;
b. Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level to the Sub-District Head; and
c. Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Urban Village Level to the Village Head/Urban Village Head.
(2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be submitted in writing, covering:
a. administration;
b. finance;
c. services; and
d. performance.
(3) Submission of written reports as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

Article 14
(1) Parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in Article 10 letter d legally have full responsibility to prevent all forms of violence, report when violence occurs and protect victims.
(2) In the event that parents, guardians and/or family as referred to in paragraph (1) do not exist or their whereabouts are unknown or due to a certain reason cannot carry out their obligations and responsibilities, then the obligations and responsibilities may transfer to the Regional Government and other family members implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 3
The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in carrying out prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and children victims of acts of violence.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

11. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
12. Violence Against Children is any act against a child that results in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, including neglect and maltreatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
13. Special Protection is a form of protection received by Children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
14. Domestic Violence hereinafter referred to as KDRT is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically, and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion, or unlawful deprivation of freedom within the household scope.
15. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
16. Guardian is a person or entity that in fact exercises parental authority as Parents over a Child.
17. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.

19. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter referred to as LSM is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own will and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare business established by the organization/institution as a manifestation of community participation in efforts to improve community welfare that emphasizes voluntary service.
20. Victim is a woman and child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence occurring in the Garut Regency area.
21. Prevention is an effort to develop the capacity and mechanisms of the Regional Government and community in creating conditions that can prevent the occurrence of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation and/or neglect.
22. Handling is action that includes identification, rescue, rehabilitation and reintegration of women and children who are victims of acts of violence, maltreatment, KDRT, exploitation, maltreatment or neglect.
23. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
24. Service is action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against victims will, is or has occurred.
25. Assistance is an effort made by a person or representative from an institution that has expertise in assisting victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

SANCTIONS
Article 41
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER XII
SANCTIONS
Article 41
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of providing protection, that does not carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 36
(1) The Regional Government establishes partnerships with the business sector, NGOs/social organizations concerned with women and children in the protection of women and children against acts of violence.
(2) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of violence;
b. education and training for women and children victims of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and increasing the economic independence of women victims of violence.
(3) Partnerships as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are set forth in the form of agreements in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 12

d. allocate budget for the protection of women and children from violence in accordance with the village's financial capacity.
(2) In order to carry out the obligations and responsibilities as referred to in paragraph (1), the Village Government prepares programs and activities for the protection of women and children in the village action plan which is part of the Village Medium-Term Development Plan (RPJMDes).

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.

(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;

c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or

CHAPTER XII
SANCTIONS
Article 41
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of providing protection, that does not carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 28
Increasing resilience as referred to in Article 27 letter a is carried out by providing guidance and assistance for strengthening mental spirituality.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 24
(1) Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in Article 19 letter a number 5 are carried out to return victims to their families and social environment.
(2) Repatriation and social reintegration services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by the Regional Government in coordination with:
a. Regency/City Government within one Provincial territory or outside the Province; and/or
b. related agencies and institutions both Government and non-Government.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER XII
SANCTIONS
Article 41
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of providing protection, that does not carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 3
The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in carrying out prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and children victims of acts of violence.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

CHAPTER XII
SANCTIONS
Article 41
(1) Every person who intentionally does not provide protection to women and children resulting in the occurrence of violence, allows the occurrence of violence, and/or does not report and does not provide protection to victims, shall be subject to sanctions as stipulated in the applicable laws and regulations.
(2) Regency Regional Apparatus that has the duties and functions of providing protection, that does not carry out its obligations and responsibilities shall be subject to administrative sanctions.
(3) The Management of P2TP2A, the Task Force for the Protection of Women and Children at the Sub-District Level, the Task Unit for the Protection of Women and Children at the Village/Sub-District Level and other institutions or organizations in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations that carry out protection duties, if they violate protection principles, may be subject to sanctions in accordance with the mechanisms applicable within their respective institutions or organizations.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 3
The purpose of the regulation regarding the protection of women and children from acts of violence is to provide guidance and direction for the Regional Government and the community in carrying out prevention, services and social rehabilitation of women and children victims of acts of violence.

CHAPTER VII

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.
(6) Other violence as referred to in Article 6 letter f constitutes threats of violence and coercion.
(7) Threats of violence as referred to in paragraph (6) include any unlawful act in the form of speech, writing, images, symbols, or body movements, whether with or without using means that cause fear or restrict a person's fundamental freedom.
(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.

Article 26
(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 15 letter c constitutes services provided by companions to restore the traumatic condition of victims.

a. providing guidance and counseling to victims and parents of victims;
b. psychological recovery of victims;
c. accompanying victims and parents of victims in the family and community environment; and
d. providing safe houses for victims of violence who require continuous handling.
(3) Special social rehabilitation for female victims of domestic violence and human trafficking is carried out by:
a. providing guidance and counseling;
b. psychological recovery of victims; and
c. accompanying victims in the family and community environment.
(4) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus having principal tasks and functions in the fields of:
a. social affairs;
b. women's empowerment and child protection;
c. health; and
d. mental and spiritual.
(5) In addition to being implemented by the Regency Regional Apparatus as referred to in paragraph (4), social rehabilitation may also be implemented by the community or social service institutions.

Article 7
(1) Physical violence as referred to in Article 6 letter a constitutes an act that results in pain accompanied by injury, wounds or disability to the body, miscarriage, loss of consciousness and/or causes death of women and/or children.
(2) Psychological violence as referred to in Article 6 letter b constitutes an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or psychological suffering of women and/or children.
(3) Sexual violence as referred to in Article 6 letter c, includes: a. acts in the form of sexual harassment, consisting of:
1) physical harassment;
2) verbal harassment;
3) gestural harassment;
4) written or pictorial harassment; and
5) psychological/emotional harassment.
b. forced sexual intercourse;
c. forced sexual intercourse in an unnatural or unwanted manner; and/or
d. forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
(4) Neglect as referred to in Article 6 letter d, includes:
a. acts that result in the unfulfillment of a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care;
b. acts of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or look after a child as appropriate, committed by parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for their care; and/or
c. acts of deliberately neglecting women within the scope of their household, whereas according to the law applicable to them or due to agreement or contract they are obligated to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to such women.
(5) Exploitation as referred to in Article 6 letter e, includes:
a. acts of exploiting economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others;
b. acts with or without the consent of the victim which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial; and
c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of the victim to obtain benefits, but not limited to prostitution or indecent acts.

(8) Coercion as referred to in paragraph (6) includes a situation where a person/victim is ordered to do something in such a way that the person does something contrary to their own will.
